correctness.rationale: For all 0<alpha<1, 0<epsilon<1/2 and p in [epsilon,1-epsilon], log2 radius after n steps equals 2^n(t-S_n); atomlessness follows from cylinders <=(1-epsilon)^n. The prefix-tail factorization is exact up to null binary boundary words. Along all ones/zeros the affine clipped state reaches an absorbing endpoint in finitely many same-digit steps, yielding the two stated identities and a common reflected tail CDF. Uniform cylinder lower bounds and finite uniform saturation give two-sided radial power comparability. Exact dyadic thresholds show exponent optimal. The rational two-digit calculation H(3/4)=27/32 and the strict square-root comparison prove nonconstant normalized phases. The accompanying executed rational checker tests 70 finite equalities; those checks are supplemental to the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 clipped random-polynomial example is motivated by restoration of continuity under state truncation; its actual continuity modulus and boundary asymptotics are left unspecified. This theorem identifies the exact sharp endpoint exponent, independence from the reinforcement parameter, uniformity over initial state, a shared finite-onset dyadic shape at both boundaries, and a rigorous non-power oscillation witness. The result answers a natural regularity question and provides a precise benchmark for related state-dependent random dynamical systems; it is not a cosmetic reformulation of continuity or a numerical slice.
